  - because: Backing the home side of the moneyline because 2 pre-registered signals fired: (1) this lineup's measured production against the primary pitch of the starter it faces (lineup_vs_primary_pitch; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.275 wOBA, home 0.369 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 826 plate appearances; home over 3,318 plate appearances); a gap of 0.094 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.092 wOBA (rung 3 of 3, the 90th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,048 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. This is a signal count, not a forecast: it publishes no probability of its own, says nothing about whether the market's price is mistaken, and attaches no claim of value -- none has been earned.   - because: Backing the away side of the moneyline because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (lineup_platoon_share; each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 88.9%, home 55.6% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 33.3 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24).
